title: The Fountainhead
author: Ayn Rand
summary: An uncompromising young architect refuses to design anything but what he believes in, even when it costs him commissions and friends. The novel sets him against a world of conformity and compromise.
readIf: you like long, polemical novels about individualism, whether you agree with them or not.
skipIf: you dislike lecturing, or want complex, believable characters, since many of them stand for ideas.

pairings.reason: The author's even longer and more explicit statement of the same philosophy, as a dystopian thriller.
A short, elegant novel about ambition and image that is much more doubtful about its hero.
Offers a deeply different view of society, about collective struggle rather than the lone genius.
